newsitem.title: USA: Telescan sees significant improvement in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Telescan sees significant improvement in Q3.

text.p: Telescan Inc, reporting second-quarter earnings Wednesday, said it expected to see "significant improvement" in the third quarter.
The operator of on-line networks posted a net income of $169,000, or $0.02 a share, in the second quarter, compared with a $940,000 loss, or $0.09 a share, a year earlier.
Telescan attributed the gain mostly to private-label agreements with financial services companies and growing popularity of its Wall Street City Internet site.
The company said its second-quarter results included a loss af almost $0.02 a share at its subsidiary Knowledge Express Data Systems of Berwyn, Pa.

Chief executive David Brown said in a statement Telescan is continuing to reduce the negative impact of Knowledge Express, a provider of research databases, and expects to see significant improvement in the third quarter.
"We expect initiatives launched in the second quarter will build on the momentum created in the past year and contribute to our third-quarter performance," Brown said.

Telescan's second-quarter revenues rose 31 percent to $4.2 million from $3.2 million a year earlier. Service revenues jumped 40 percent to $3.4 million, while other revenues rose to $866,000 from $834,000. The company said its operating expenses declined three percent to $4.2 million.
The company's stock closed at 5-1/8 Tuesday.
